item.title: [9] Quantum geometry in the NbSe2 family: Obstructed compact Wannier function and perturbation theory
item.description:
Last authors: Fernando De Juan, B. Andrei Bernevig

Authors: Jiabin Yu, Yi Jiang, Yuanfeng Xu, et al.

Score 9/10 B_IMPORTANT_CONDMAT

Why: High relevance to NbSe2 electronic structure and charge order/superconductivity.

Tags: #NbSe2 #electronicstructure #superconductivity

Abstract: Here, the authors reveal that monolayer NbSe 2 and related transition metal dichalcogenides host obstructed atomic bands near the Fermi level. By constructing a b i n i t i o six-, three-, and single-band Wannier models, they identify remarkably compact obstructed Wannier functions and an unusual dominance of next-nearest-neighbor hopping. These results provide a transparent low-energy framework for investigating how quantum geometry shapes charge order, electron–phonon coupling, and superconductivity in NbSe 2 .

item.title: [7] Incommensurate antiferromagnetism with amplitude modulation in the semiconducting 5f van der Waals magnet α−UTe3
item.description:
Last authors: Yo Tokunaga, Yoshinori Haga

Authors: Hironori Sakai, Chihiro Tabata, Koji Kaneko, et al.

Score 7/10 B_IMPORTANT_CONDMAT

Why: Van der Waals magnetic systems relevant to electronic and structural characterization.

Tags: #vanderWaals #magnetism #neutron

Abstract: Here, the authors combine nuclear magnetic resonance and single-crystal neutron diffraction to constrain a plausible magnetic structure model for the incommensurate antiferromagnetic state of the semiconducting 5 f van der Waals magnet α -UTe 3 . The model captures strong spin anisotropy and spatially modulated ordered moments, suggesting that this unusual order develops near a quantum critical point associated with crystal-field singlet induced magnetism in a layered actinide system with highly anisotropic 5 f electrons.

item.title: [7] Coexistence of magnon and spinon excitations in SeCuO3
item.description:
Last authors: Raman Sankar, Kwang-Yong Choi

Authors: Youngsu Choi, Dirk Wulferding, Kalaivanan Raju, Raman Sankar, Kwang-Yong Choi

Score 7/10 B_IMPORTANT_CONDMAT

Why: Relevant to quasi-1D materials and spin-charge separation physics.

Tags: #quasi-1D #spinon #magnon

Abstract: Using temperature-, field-, and angle-dependent Raman scattering, the authors observe here a sharp magnon coexisting with a broad spinon continuum in the quasi-one-dimensional quantum magnet SeCuO 3 . Both excitations exhibit identical angular dependence governed by the same Raman scattering symmetry. This common scattering symmetry demonstrates that coherent magnons emerge from the confinement of fractionalized spinons inherent to a one-dimensional quantum magnet.

item.title: [8] X-ray imaging of antiferromagnetic cluster octupole domains in Mn3Sn
item.description:
Last authors: T. Arima, Y. Tokura

Authors: M. T. Birch, S. Wintz, Y. Sun, et al.

Score 8/10 B_IMPORTANT_CONDMAT

Why: Magnetic topological materials and Hall effect mechanisms are very relevant.

Tags: #Mn3Sn #anomalousHall #imaging

Abstract: Here, the authors use element-specific x-ray microscopy to image antiferromagnetic cluster octupole domain structures in focused ion-beam fabricated Mn 3 Sn devices. The magnetic contrast arises from pre-edge x-ray magnetic circular dichroism that is independent of the small net moment, revealing how mesoscale textures evolve under applied magnetic fields and link to the anomalous Hall response. The results establish x-ray microscopy as a powerful route to image domain structures in time-reversal symmetry breaking antiferromagnets.

item.title: [8] Quantum oscillation fingerprints of altermagnetism in hole-doped RuO2
item.description:
Last authors: Yuchi Yang, Yusheng Hou

Score 8/10 B_IMPORTANT_CONDMAT

Why: Altermagnetism and Fermi surface physics via quantum oscillations are highly relevant.

Tags: #altermagnet #Fermisurface #quantumoscillation

Abstract: Here, the authors focus on a representative pair of simple closed-pocket Fermi surfaces in hole-doped RuO 2 and establish a quasilinear correlation between the local magnetic moment of Ru atoms and quantum-oscillation-based signature of spin splitting. Combined with the distinct quantum oscillation characteristics of the nonmagnetic, intermediate, and stable altermagnetic regimes, this correlation provides experimentally accessible fingerprints for identifying magnetic states and tracking altermagnetic spin splitting in hole-doped RuO 2 .

item.title: [8] Yu-Shiba-Rusinov states in Ising superconductors
item.description:
Last authors: Juan Carlos Cuevas, Wolfgang Belzig

Authors: Michael Hein, Juan Carlos Cuevas, Wolfgang Belzig

Score 8/10 B_IMPORTANT_CONDMAT

Why: STM and magnetic impurity probes of 2D superconductors; highly relevant spectroscopy context.

Tags: #theory #STM #superconductivity #2Dmaterials

Abstract: Ising superconductors are two-dimensional materials that can host an unconventional superconducting state stabilized by strong spin-valley locking. Here, the authors theoretically propose the use of magnetic impurities as local probes of the superconducting state by studying Yu-Shiba-Rusinov bound states. They identify experimentally accessible signatures, including the bound-state spectrum and the supercurrent between the sample and a superconducting STM tip.

item.title: [9] Phonon scattering mechanisms in WTe2 observed by ultrafast coherent phonon spectroscopy
item.description:
Last authors: Yu Mizukoshi, Muneaki Hase

Authors: Mizuki Akei, Yu Mizukoshi, Muneaki Hase

Score 9/10 B_IMPORTANT_CONDMAT

Why: Experimental investigation of Weyl semimetal WTe2 and its electronic structure/Lifshitz transition.; demoted from A: broad CM, not direct user/project hit

Tags: #experiment #Weylsemimetal #ultrafast #WTe2

Abstract: T d -WTe 2 is a Weyl semimetal, which exhibits unique physical properties of electronic states, such as the Lifshitz transition. Here, using ultrafast laser spectroscopy, the authors reveal contribution of phonon-electron scattering only for the low-frequency A 1 optical phonon, in addition to conventional phonon-phonon scattering at low temperatures. The findings of the phonon-electron scattering path possibly induced by the Lifshitz transition pave the way for further exploration of the electronic structure and transport properties in a wide range of quantum materials.

item.title: [7] Hybrid light-matter excitations and spontaneous time-reversal symmetry breaking in two-dimensional Josephson junctions
item.description:
Last authors: V. Varrica, G. Falci, E. Paladino, and F. M. D. Pellegrino

Score 7/10 B_IMPORTANT_CONDMAT

Why: Theoretical study of spontaneous TRSB in superconductors/Josephson junctions.

Tags: #TRSB #superconductivity #Josephsonjunction

Abstract: Here, the authors show that inductive coupling between a superconducting resonator and a short, wide two-dimensional material-based Josephson junction induces a phase transition in the global light–matter ground state. The resulting phase, which spontaneously breaks time-reversal symmetry, carries a finite equilibrium supercurrent at phase difference ϕ = π , where an isolated conventional Josephson junction carries no equilibrium supercurrent. The hybrid light–matter excitation spectrum provides spectroscopic fingerprints of the transition, while highly transparent transport channels determine the critical coupling.
